Rushes

A film discovery interface that presents one trailer per screen, records a binary preference for each title, and reports where the film can be streamed, rented or bought in the viewer’s country.

Visit the site ↗How to useEngineering record

Engineering recordFor technical reviewers

Built a film-discovery feed on one serverless function: the server shapes everything the page needs from TMDB into one response, and the client stays a single page without a framework or an account.

System architecture

Client
  • Endless trailer feed
  • YouTube embed, muted by default
  • Saved and hidden lists on device
JSON
Server
  • Vercel function: query by year and genre
  • Keep titles with a trailer, merge details
REST
External services
  • TMDB
  • JustWatch via TMDB

The page asks the function for a batch. The function queries TMDB by year and genre, drops films without a trailer, and fetches trailer, credits, budget and watch providers for the viewer’s country, returning one compact payload so the client makes a single request per batch.

Key engineering decisions

01

A backend-for-frontend of one function

Aggregating several TMDB calls on the server hides the key and turns many round trips into one, which matters on mobile.

02

No account

Lists live on the device, so there is no personal data to store or secure.

Notes for reviewers

Limits and next stepsAdd edge caching of batches by year and genre to cut TMDB calls, and a share link for a saved list.
01

Problem statement

Choosing a film on a streaming service is slow. Each service shows only its own catalogue, in rows of small posters, and finding where a given title is available means leaving for another site.

02

Contribution

Rushes shows one film per screen; its trailer starts on arrival, and one scroll brings the next title. The viewer marks each film Watch it, which saves it to a list, or Not for me, which hides it. A panel lists the services that carry the film in the viewer’s country, with plot, fact sheet, cast and crew, further clips and similar titles. A section for filmmakers adds notes on structure, writing, cinematography, editing, sound, design, performance and producing.

03

Architecture

A single page without a framework. A Vercel function queries TMDB by year and genre, keeps the titles that have a trailer, and returns trailer, credits, budget and providers in one response, so the API key stays on the server. Trailers play through the YouTube embedded player, muted until the viewer turns the sound on. The saved list and the hidden titles are stored on the device, and no account is created.

04

Verification and limitations

Film data and images come from TMDB and availability from JustWatch; Rushes is endorsed by neither, and its availability information is only as current as those sources.
